definition: Tiny always-on models that detect a trigger phrase on-device under severe compute, memory, and power constraints, with false-accept and false-reject rates as the core tradeoff.
details: Tiny always-on models that detect a trigger phrase on-device under severe compute, memory, and power constraints, with false-accept and false-reject rates as the core tradeoff. The gateway component of every voice assistant.

explainer.lead: Tiny always-on models that listen for a trigger phrase on-device under tight compute, memory and power limits. It is the gateway to every voice assistant.

tiers.eli5: Like a doorman who only listens for your name and ignores everything else, so the heavy machinery inside never has to wake up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers trade false accepts against false rejects at a fixed power budget, often running a small model continuously. The pitfall is tuning thresholds on clean data and getting spurious wake-ups in noisy rooms.
tiers.paperLevel: A binary detection task on streaming audio with strict latency and energy constraints; performance is reported as false-accept and false-reject rates, and the two trade off against each other. Accuracy degrades with noise and accents.

explainer.example: A phone wakes when it hears its wake word, then hands the audio to a larger speech model for the actual command.
